rules.statement: Enforce tenant isolation for tenant-owned data at the persistence layer with a global query filter on the data context, not by loading a resource and then comparing its tenant id to the request's tenant.
rules.why: A post-fetch check materializes another tenant's (possibly sensitive) data before the scope decision, so a log statement, early return or refactor in that window can leak it; per-call-site scoped getters leak on a single omission.
rules.check: Look for code that fetches a tenant-bound entity by id and then compares `entity.TenantId` to the resolved tenant (or calls a boundary/guard helper after the fetch), or new repository methods that take the tenant as a parameter instead of relying on the ambient query filter.

rules.statement: Make every new tenant-owned entity, including child rows such as secrets and settings, implement the tenant-entity marker so that the tenant query filter covers it, and leave only the tenant root and global (server-level) data outside the filter.
rules.why: New tenant-bound resource families get isolation only by joining the filtered set; an entity left out is readable across tenants.
rules.check: A new entity with an owning-tenant relationship that doesn't implement the tenant-scoped marker interface or doesn't get the global query filter in the model configuration.

rules.statement: Write the tenant query filter as 'ambient tenant is unset OR the row's denormalized, indexed tenant discriminator column equals the ambient tenant', not as a navigation or join to the tenant entity.
rules.why: A single indexed-column predicate is cheap and keeps the persistence framework decoupled from the concrete tenant entity, and the unset case keeps the filter a no-op for the runtime and central-admin surfaces.
rules.check: A `HasQueryFilter` on a tenant-owned entity that navigates to the tenant entity, uses a non-indexed column, or lacks the 'no ambient tenant' branch.

rules.statement: Take the owning tenant of a newly created tenant-bound resource from the request's resolved ambient tenant scope, and never accept a tenant identifier in the create request contract.
rules.why: A tenant-bound resource is always owned by the request's tenant; echoing a client-supplied tenant is redundant and a footgun, while deriving it means a caller can only create within its own tenant.
rules.check: Create request DTOs that carry a tenant id field, or create handlers that set the owning tenant from request input rather than the ambient tenant accessor.

rules.statement: Don't add a separate 'parent tenant exists' lookup to create validation when the request's tenant scope was opened from a tenant the resolver already loaded from the store.
rules.why: Opening the scope already proves the tenant exists, so a second lookup is a redundant round-trip for a row that was just loaded.
rules.check: Create validators for tenant-bound resources that query the store to check that the owning tenant exists.

rules.statement: Set the ambient tenant scope once per request in a reusable endpoint filter on the tenant-bound route group, for every tenant strategy including static single-tenant, and short-circuit with the mapped result (typically 404) when the tenant can't be resolved.
rules.why: Setting it once in a shared filter means no per-endpoint logic is needed and new endpoints inherit isolation; skipping it for one strategy would leave those requests unscoped.
rules.check: Tenant-bound endpoints that resolve the tenant or open the scope themselves, endpoints added outside the scoped route group, or conditional logic that skips the scope for some tenant strategies.

rules.statement: Store the ambient tenant scope in an `AsyncLocal<T>`, not in a scoped DI service, so it flows across async calls to data contexts created by a factory from the root provider.
rules.why: Data contexts made by `IDbContextFactory` from the root provider live outside the request's DI scope, so a DI-scoped holder would leave them unscoped.
rules.check: An ambient tenant accessor implementation that keeps the current tenant in a scoped-service field or `HttpContext` item instead of an `AsyncLocal<T>`.

rules.statement: Make the data context require a non-null tenant accessor, represent the 'no tenant' state as a null tenant id on the accessor, and have tests or tooling that build the context directly pass an explicit no-tenant accessor.
rules.why: A required dependency fails fast at startup when it isn't registered, instead of silently running without tenant isolation (fail-closed against cross-tenant leaks).
rules.check: A data context constructor parameter for the tenant accessor that is nullable or optional, null-coalescing around a missing accessor, or tests passing `null` for it.

rules.statement: Treat a tenant-bound resource owned by another tenant as not found (404) by loading it through the tenant-filtered query, so the null result is returned before validation runs, and don't return a distinct forbidden response.
rules.why: A cross-tenant resource should be unreachable and indistinguishable from a missing one, so nothing about it can be logged, inspected or returned.
rules.check: Get, update or delete handlers for tenant-bound resources that return 403 or another distinct error for cross-tenant ids, or that run validation before the tenant-filtered lookup.
